examples.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/040ac76a28687db1c99d3379242b726a85aa4baf269a7c6d35d9662af1d3bd78.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/2ee58da2733a468406869e43f57deebc6f7924f1d1149c0ca9391ea9995d9f87.png)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/83596c7f3038e585eb35ffafc966810e6891b55fc4d1efb04494bdc4b3755b05.png)

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=4$ with the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/af5b69c599a13a707365e88f6f50939064c7b199a1d8231b32a1c88e425440fa.png)

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=-6$ with the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/833ce06c0c6d5f9beea87a84ef1b286748472c312987e837ca6f47f60225b1fa.png)

The general solution of the system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/fb015d0935718dd6ffdfb9eb13b2b8fd0c255c63a2f5cecdb988a3f83df14685.png)

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/03f2711cb5a80e1e94f879bf8a68c25db27f8280f5e1e344425f9ee2a334a829.png)
lie on the $x$-axis. Since $e^{4t} \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t \to \infty.$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/bd4d36cd68896e6360317a0c01c92841423020218436d85ae07eb413463fffa8.png)
lie on the $y$-axis. Since $e^{-6t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$

Among the given options, the only phase portrait satisfying these conditions is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/91c074766b92790a0e78b768b0290d7723617d6ed30e51e842501cad63e58a44.png)
